terms.metaDescription: Review the open-source license, service configuration, content management, and backup guidance for VOZEB PRO.
terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.subtitle: Before using, deploying, or extending VOZEB PRO, please make sure you understand the open-source license, service configuration responsibilities, content compliance, and upgrade/backup requirements.
terms.section1Body: VOZEB PRO is an open-source project for AI creation, canvas, prompt management, and asset accumulation. You may deploy, modify, and distribute it as long as you comply with the AGPL-3.0 license and the original author's attribution requirements.
terms.section2Body: Deployers must configure and manage AI interfaces, model services, email SMTP, and third-party storage services themselves, and comply with the corresponding providers' terms. Issues caused by external interfaces, model output, email services, or the deployment environment should be assessed and handled by the deployer.
terms.section3Body: Administrators can manage users, quotas, registration policies, email services, site information, and the public prompt library. Do not upload, generate, or spread illegal, infringing, malicious content, or content that violates local laws and regulations.
terms.section4Body: This project is still under active development. Before upgrading, export desensitized business data from the admin console first, and separately back up PostgreSQL, payment records, the server media directory, and external object storage according to your deployment method.

privacy.metaDescription: Learn how VOZEB PRO handles account, creation, media, and third-party service data.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: This page explains how VOZEB PRO handles data for accounts, email, model requests, and backup files, so deployers and users can understand the boundaries in advance.
privacy.section1Body: VOZEB PRO stores accounts, projects, creative conversations, generation records, and media files on the server. Media is categorized as temporary or long-term, and administrators can manage and delete it in the admin console.
privacy.section2Body: When email registration, email change, or password recovery is enabled, the system sends verification codes through the SMTP service configured by the administrator. Codes are used only to verify the current action, are valid for 10 minutes by default, and expire after use.
privacy.section3Body: AI generation requests are all sent through the system's interface proxy to the model service or OpenAI-compatible interface configured by the administrator; the client never sees the real upstream domain or API key. Deployers should still confirm the data handling policies of the corresponding providers.
privacy.section4Body: Administrators can export desensitized business data from the admin console. Exports do not include emails, password hashes, sessions, verification codes, CDKs, channel keys, payment configuration, external storage credentials, or original media files; the full database and media are still backed up by the deployer via local, Docker, Baota, or cloud solutions.

install.wizardSubtitle: Complete server setup in three steps
install.stepLockedHint: Finish database and encryption configuration first

intro.title: Confirm the setup process first
intro.description: {site} is built for server deployment; business data is stored in PostgreSQL. The wizard will guide you through generating configuration, checking initialization status, and creating the first administrator account.
intro.process1Text: Use localhost for local deployment; postgres for the bundled Docker database; 127.0.0.1 for a Baota host database; use the provider's connection address for a cloud database.
intro.process2Text: The setup page never saves your database password. Copy the generated configuration and write it into .env.local, Docker Compose, or your server's environment variables.
intro.process3Text: Run the restart command shown for your deployment method, then refresh the check once the service is back up; after the connection succeeds, manually initialize the schema and create an administrator.
intro.footerHint: If you've already configured the database, this page will show the current initialization status directly.

database.title: Configure and initialize the database
database.description: Fill in the database details, copy the configuration, write it into server environment variables, and restart the web service. The status check only verifies the connection; you explicitly initialize the schema once it looks correct.
database.waitingTitle: Waiting for database and encryption key
database.nextStep1: Restart the application using the command for your current deployment method on the left.
database.nextStep2: Wait 10-30 seconds, then click "Refresh check" below.
database.nextStep3: Once you see "Database connected", click "Initialize schema".
database.nextStep4: After initialization succeeds, move on to creating the administrator.

admin.notReadyDescription: The database schema or the encryption key isn't ready yet, so you can't create an administrator account.
admin.readyDescription: The site setup is complete. You can now go to the admin console to configure model channels, plan benefits, and payment channels.
admin.firstAdminNoteTitle: The first account automatically becomes administrator
admin.firstAdminNoteText: You'll be taken straight to the admin console after creation. Subsequent user registrations will follow the admin registration policy.

local.label: Local
local.description: Web and PostgreSQL both run directly on the current system without Docker; configuration is saved to web/.env.local.

docker.label: Docker
docker.description: Web and the bundled PostgreSQL run in separate containers, started together by the default docker-compose.yml.

baota.label: Baota
baota.description: Web runs in a container and connects to a PostgreSQL instance already installed on the Baota host; no additional database is started.

cloud.label: Cloud database
cloud.description: Web connects to a remote PostgreSQL hosted by a cloud provider; enter the provider's address and enable SSL as required.

database2.snippetEnvDescription: Environment variables the app needs to connect to the database
database2.snippetComposeDescription: Used to start or rebuild the application container
database2.snippetSqlDescription: Run in the database server terminal to create a dedicated account and database
database2.sslHint: Enable when required by your cloud database provider
database2.fieldNoteHostPortText: Use 127.0.0.1 for a Baota host database; use postgres for the bundled Docker database.
database2.fieldNoteDatabaseUserText: We recommend a dedicated database and account to avoid mixing with other projects in the same PostgreSQL instance.
database2.fieldNotePasswordText: The setup page only generates configuration text; it never saves the database password in the browser or on the server.
database2.fieldNoteEncryptionKeyText: A random 32-byte key is generated; it must stay unchanged after deployment, or previously saved secrets can no longer be decrypted.
database2.copyConfigDesc: View one complete configuration block at a time, avoiding narrow columns and horizontal scrolling.
database2.passwordMissingText: Please fill in the Password field above first. The encryption key has been generated automatically; the copy button will be enabled once the password is filled in.

local.step1Text: Copy the "create-database command" and run it in your local PostgreSQL terminal; skip this if the database and account already exist.
local.step2Text: Copy the "environment variables" and save them as a .env.local file in the project's web directory.
local.step3Text: Stop the old process, then restart it from the web directory so the environment variables take effect.
local.step4Text: Refresh the setup page, and once connected click "Initialize schema", then create an administrator.

docker.step1Text: Copy the "environment variables" and save them to the project root .env; the bundled PostgreSQL will be created automatically by Compose.
docker.step2Text: Use the project's bundled docker-compose.yml, or copy the Compose template above to overwrite your deployment configuration.
docker.step3Text: Run the command in the project root and wait for the containers to become healthy.
docker.step4Text: Refresh the setup page, and once the database connection is confirmed click "Initialize schema", then create an administrator.

baota.step1Text: Open the "create-database command" above, copy it, and run it in the Baota "Terminal". Skip this if the database and account already exist.
baota.step2Text: Copy the "environment variables" and create or update the .env file under /www/wwwroot/vozeb-pro.
baota.step3Text: In the Baota terminal, go to the project directory and run the command below so the new environment variables actually take effect.
baota.step4Text: Wait 10-30 seconds, then click "Refresh check" on the right; once connected, click "Initialize schema".

cloud.step1Text: Create the database and account in your cloud database console first, and allow your app server's IP as required by the provider.
cloud.step2Text: Copy the "environment variables" to the project root .env; keep "Enable SSL" on if required by the provider.
cloud.step3Text: Recreate the application container so DATABASE_URL and the encryption key take effect.
cloud.step4Text: Refresh the setup page, and once connected click "Initialize schema", then create an administrator.
